title: Local preservation of homology carries homology isomorphisms to homology isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. A short complex $V$ means three objects and maps $V^-\xrightarrow{u_V}V^0\xrightarrow{v_V}V^+$ with $v_Vu_V=0$. Choose a kernel $i_V:Z_V\to V^0$ of $v_V$, let $\bar u_V:V^-\to Z_V$ be the unique map with $i_V\bar u_V=u_V$, and choose a cokernel $q_V:Z_V\to H(V)$ of $\bar u_V$. A morphism $a:S\to T$ of short complexes is a triple of maps commuting with $u$ and $v$; $H(a)$ is the induced map on these cokernels.

Let $S,T$ be short complexes. For each $V=S,T$, assume that $F(i_V):F(Z_V)\to F(V^0)$ is a kernel of $F(v_V)$ and that $F(q_V):F(Z_V)\to F(H(V))$ is a cokernel of $F(\bar u_V)$. These hypotheses concern only the two specified kernel and two specified cokernel diagrams; $F$ need not preserve any other kernel or cokernel.

There are canonical isomorphisms $c_V:H(FV)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(H(V))$ induced by these kernel and cokernel diagrams. For every morphism $a:S\to T$ they satisfy
$$
c_T\circ H(Fa)=F(H(a))\circ c_S.
$$
If $H(a)$ is an isomorphism, then $H(Fa)$ is an isomorphism, and
$$
H(Fa)=c_T^{-1}\circ F(H(a))\circ c_S.
$$

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line for each clause: the chosen kernel/cokernel hypotheses are LeftHomologyData.IsPreservedBy (lines 69-79); CategoryTheory.Functor.PreservesLeftHomologyOf.mk' (line 303) converts each chosen datum into PreservesLeftHomologyOf. CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso (line 455) is c_V; mapHomologyIso_hom_naturality (line 616) is the displayed naturality formula. CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.quasiIso_map_of_preservesLeftHomology (line 811) is the final implication, with ShortComplex.QuasiIso meaning invertibility of homologyMap. All four short complexes have homology because the categories are abelian. The conjugation formula is the naturality equality composed with c_T inverse.
